1	# Growth — extract lessons (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's capture stage, over **both** lesson sources in one run: the window's repo activity
4	(commits, merged PRs, issue discussion) and the conversation logs captured from working sessions. Each
5	durable, reusable lesson is folded into the repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/` — the
6	normalized capture surface) at the repo's own level, without straining to generalize it. The run lands its
7	edits through a single PR **delivered to land** (on the default delivery settings it merges once the repo's
8	checks pass, with no human review — daily capture never piles up as review requests); finding nothing to add
9	on a given run is a perfectly good outcome.
10	
11	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding
12	scope**: it names which halves are live, the substantive commit shas and the PRs/issues touched in the
13	window, and whether the retention prune is due. That is the work; do not widen it.
14	
15	> This is the **unattended daily** capture. It writes only the repo's *own* local packs, so — **unlike** an
16	> owner-requested, in-session retrospective (which delivers a PR for a human to review) — it opens a PR and
17	> **delivers it to land** (the shared procedure under *Output* below; on the default settings GitHub lands it
18	> once the repo's checks pass). The shared canon stays human-gated — lifting anything up into it is the
19	> central promote task's job (canon-side), and that PR waits for the owner.
20	
21	## Conventions used in this doc
22	
23	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
24	- **Access split — local git for repo content, MCP for the issue/PR API.** The repo's own content is plain
25	  **local git** in the checkout: the commits, the `conversation-logs` branch and its files
26	  (`git fetch`/`show`/`rm`/`push`), and staging the lesson edits onto a branch. Reading issue/PR activity,
27	  opening the PR and delivering it, posting the exchange summaries and the tracking-issue log go
28	  through the session's **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub
29	  access — the shell reaches only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so
30	  never reach for `gh`/`curl` or a cross-repo clone.
31	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in
32	  [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) — everything
33	  under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
34	  window), the repo's own packs; never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
35	
36	## The run — two source skills, then the upgrade pass
37	
38	The **method** for each source lives in its skill; this worker only frames the run around them. Don't
39	re-derive any of it here.
40	
41	1. **Activity half — the [extract-from-activity](../../skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) skill**, over
42	   exactly the commits, merged PRs and issues named in Context. **Skip this half entirely when Context says
43	   the activity half is not in scope** (a quiet repo whose only reason to run was the retention prune).
44	2. **Conversation half — the [extract-from-conversations](../../skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
45	   skill**, over the repo's captured logs. `git fetch origin conversation-logs`, then list its files
46	   (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/conversation-logs`); no branch, or no `*.jsonl`, and this half is done.
47	   Give each log captured in the recent window a **fresh pass** (its filename carries the capture stamp;
48	   corpus dedup makes an overlapping re-read harmless, so err toward re-reading the last several days), and
49	   post the skill's provenance summary for each rule that actually lands.
50	3. **Retention prune**, when Context says it is due. Read `retention_days` from this repo's
51	   `.claudinite-checks.json` (the grow_with_claudinite entry's `config.retention_days`) — unset means this
52	   step is skipped entirely (capture-only adoption). For each log whose filename stamp is older than
53	   `retention_days` days: give it the **final hindsight pass** the skill describes (anything it still yields
54	   lands like any other keeper), then `git rm` it on the `conversation-logs` branch and push (commit message
55	   ending `[skip ci]`). The branch is never merged and its history is never rewritten — plain add/remove
56	   commits only. This push to the non-default logs branch is outside the outcome taxonomy (DESIGN §1).
57	4. **Upgrade pass — the [prose-to-checks](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill, over what *this run*
58	   just wrote.** Both halves route down the local promotion ladder as they go, but a lesson written as prose
59	   under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides. So before opening the PR, take the prose
60	   this run added and ask the skill's questions of it: does it clear the working-rule gate, and does it
61	   constrain a static signature a check could observe? If yes, convert it now — author the rule module,
62	   register it in its pack's `pack.mjs`, prove it with a **see-it-fail** fixture, and apply the deletion
63	   test to the prose the check now stands beside. **Scope is this run's own additions only** — the standing
64	   prose backlog is the weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)'s job, and widening
65	   into it here would duplicate that task's work under an auto-merging PR.
66	
67	If an edit touches something a test reads (a doc constant, a code path), run the repo's offline test suite
68	and keep it green before opening the PR.
69	
70	## Output: one PR, delivered to land
71	
72	If the run found at least one genuinely new lesson, it lands **all** of it — both halves, plus any check the
73	upgrade pass produced — through a **single PR**: one commit for the whole run on a per-run-unique branch, not
74	one per lesson and not one per half. Open the PR (title `Claudinite growth: extract lessons`, its commit
75	referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate passes), then **deliver it by the shared
76	procedure — [deliver-pr.md](../../../../engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md)**. That procedure — never this file —
77	owns every landing nuance: it reads this repo's `maintenance.delivery` (a `review` repo's PR waits for the
78	owner — still a delivered outcome), arms auto-merge where the repo allows it, and licenses the hand merge
79	when the arm is rejected `clean status` (a base branch that requires nothing — GitHub never auto-merges
80	there). Do not assume this run's PR merges unreviewed: that is the repo's setting, not this task's. On the
81	default settings it squash-merges once the repo's checks pass, so daily lesson-capture never floods review
82	requests while every change still gets a PR trail and a CI gate. This writes only the repo's *own* local
83	packs (not the shared canon). A run that finds nothing and opens nothing is fine — and common.
84	
85	A new check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one — so CI stays green and
86	the PR can merge; a check that can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
87	
88	## Tracking: log each run under the task's own issue
89	
90	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
91	
92	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract**
93	
94	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle, and it
95	differs per repo). A run that finds no issue under the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open,
96	close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no meaning, only the log does. When a run adds a lesson,
97	converts one to a check, or prunes logs, log it as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue — so the issue
98	accumulates a scrollable history, each entry naming **what happened and where**. A run that changed nothing
99	logs nothing. (A repo that still carries a closed `Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract` issue from when
100	the halves were two tasks keeps it as history — never post to it, never reopen it.)
101	
102	## Run on a capable model
103	
104	Deciding whether a lesson is genuinely new and durable — and deduping it against what's already documented —
105	is a **judgment call**, not mechanical extraction. A downgraded model adds noise or restates what's there,
106	and **on the default delivery no human reviews the PR before it lands** — CI gates correctness, not whether a
107	"lesson" earns its keep — so the capable-model requirement matters all the more. This task declares
108	`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
109	
110	## What this task must never do
111	
112	- **Never write outside the repo's own local packs** — this task improves the repo's **packs**, never the
113	  canon and never the project's own code. Everything else under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mount, and
114	  lifting a lesson up into the canon is the central promote task's job. A lesson tied to one call site lands
115	  as its pack's entry **naming the site**, not as an edit out there. The `growth-write-scope` check keys on
116	  this run's pinned title (below) and reds any path outside the local packs.
117	- **Never widen past the Context window** — the halves it declares live, the substantive commits and the
118	  touched PRs/issues named there are the scope; do not re-decide it. That includes the upgrade pass: this
119	  run's own additions, never the standing backlog.
120	- **Never merge `conversation-logs`** anywhere, and never rewrite its history — plain add and remove commits only.
121	- **Never paste the conversation onto an issue** — not raw JSONL, not a rendered transcript, not the turns
122	  themselves. Each landed rule gets one ≤200-word summary of the exchange behind it, and nothing more.
123	- **Never delete a log younger than retention, and never delete anything while `retention_days` is unset** —
124	  deletion is the ack that both passes happened.
125	- **Don't add noise** — a duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, the more so when
126	  its PR usually lands with no human review to catch it.

re-derive any of it here.

   exactly the commits, merged PRs and issues named in Context. **Skip this half entirely when Context says
   the activity half is not in scope** (a quiet repo whose only reason to run was the retention prune).

   skill**, over the repo's captured logs. `git fetch origin conversation-logs`, then list its files

packs (not the shared canon). A run that finds nothing and opens nothing is fine — and common.

accumulates a scrollable history, each entry naming **what happened and where**. A run that changed nothing
logs nothing. (A repo that still carries a closed `Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract` issue from when
the halves were two tasks keeps it as history — never post to it, never reopen it.)

is a **judgment call**, not mechanical extraction. A downgraded model adds noise or restates what's there,
and **on the default delivery no human reviews the PR before it lands** — CI gates correctness, not whether a
"lesson" earns its keep — so the capable-model requirement matters all the more. This task declares
`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Growth — extract lessons (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's capture stage, over **both** lesson sources in one run: the window's repo activity
4	(commits, merged PRs, issue discussion) and the conversation logs captured from working sessions. Each
5	durable, reusable lesson is folded into the repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/` — the
6	normalized capture surface) at the repo's own level, without straining to generalize it. The run lands its
7	edits through a single PR **delivered to land** (on the default delivery settings it merges once the repo's
8	checks pass, with no human review — daily capture never piles up as review requests); finding nothing to add
9	on a given run is a perfectly good outcome.
10	
11	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding
12	scope**: it names which halves are live, the substantive commit shas and the PRs/issues touched in the
13	window, and whether the retention prune is due. That is the work; do not widen it.
14	
15	> This is the **unattended daily** capture. It writes only the repo's *own* local packs, so — **unlike** an
16	> owner-requested, in-session retrospective (which delivers a PR for a human to review) — it opens a PR and
17	> **delivers it to land** (the shared procedure under *Output* below; on the default settings GitHub lands it
18	> once the repo's checks pass). The shared canon stays human-gated — lifting anything up into it is the
19	> central promote task's job (canon-side), and that PR waits for the owner.
20	
21	## Conventions used in this doc
22	
23	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
24	- **Access split — local git for repo content, MCP for the issue/PR API.** The repo's own content is plain
25	  **local git** in the checkout: the commits, the `conversation-logs` branch and its files
26	  (`git fetch`/`show`/`rm`/`push`), and staging the lesson edits onto a branch. Reading issue/PR activity,
27	  opening the PR and delivering it, posting the exchange summaries and the tracking-issue log go
28	  through the session's **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub
29	  access — the shell reaches only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so
30	  never reach for `gh`/`curl` or a cross-repo clone.
31	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in
32	  [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) — everything
33	  under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
34	  window), the repo's own packs; never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
35	
36	## The run — two source skills, then the upgrade pass
37	
38	The **method** for each source lives in its skill; this worker only frames the run around them. Don't
39	re-derive any of it here.
40	
41	1. **Activity half — the [extract-from-activity](../../skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) skill**, over
42	   exactly the commits, merged PRs and issues named in Context. **Skip this half entirely when Context says
43	   the activity half is not in scope** (a quiet repo whose only reason to run was the retention prune).
44	2. **Conversation half — the [extract-from-conversations](../../skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
45	   skill**, over the repo's captured logs. `git fetch origin conversation-logs`, then list its files
46	   (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/conversation-logs`); no branch, or no `*.jsonl`, and this half is done.
47	   Give each log captured in the recent window a **fresh pass** (its filename carries the capture stamp;
48	   corpus dedup makes an overlapping re-read harmless, so err toward re-reading the last several days), and
49	   post the skill's provenance summary for each rule that actually lands.
50	3. **Retention prune**, when Context says it is due. Read `retention_days` from this repo's
51	   `.claudinite-checks.json` (the grow_with_claudinite entry's `config.retention_days`) — unset means this
52	   step is skipped entirely (capture-only adoption). For each log whose filename stamp is older than
53	   `retention_days` days: give it the **final hindsight pass** the skill describes (anything it still yields
54	   lands like any other keeper), then `git rm` it on the `conversation-logs` branch and push (commit message
55	   ending `[skip ci]`). The branch is never merged and its history is never rewritten — plain add/remove
56	   commits only. This push to the non-default logs branch is outside the outcome taxonomy (DESIGN §1).
57	4. **Upgrade pass — the [prose-to-checks](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill, over what *this run*
58	   just wrote.** Both halves route down the local promotion ladder as they go, but a lesson written as prose
59	   under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides. So before opening the PR, take the prose
60	   this run added and ask the skill's questions of it: does it clear the working-rule gate, and does it
61	   constrain a static signature a check could observe? If yes, convert it now — author the rule module,
62	   register it in its pack's `pack.mjs`, prove it with a **see-it-fail** fixture, and apply the deletion
63	   test to the prose the check now stands beside. **Scope is this run's own additions only** — the standing
64	   prose backlog is the weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)'s job, and widening
65	   into it here would duplicate that task's work under an auto-merging PR.
66	
67	If an edit touches something a test reads (a doc constant, a code path), run the repo's offline test suite
68	and keep it green before opening the PR.
69	
70	## Output: one PR, delivered to land
71	
72	If the run found at least one genuinely new lesson, it lands **all** of it — both halves, plus any check the
73	upgrade pass produced — through a **single PR**: one commit for the whole run on a per-run-unique branch, not
74	one per lesson and not one per half. Open the PR (title `Claudinite growth: extract lessons`, its commit
75	referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate passes), then **deliver it by the shared
76	procedure — [deliver-pr.md](../../../../engine/scheduler/deliver-pr.md)**. That procedure — never this file —
77	owns every landing nuance: it reads this repo's `maintenance.delivery` (a `review` repo's PR waits for the
78	owner — still a delivered outcome), arms auto-merge where the repo allows it, and licenses the hand merge
79	when the arm is rejected `clean status` (a base branch that requires nothing — GitHub never auto-merges
80	there). Do not assume this run's PR merges unreviewed: that is the repo's setting, not this task's. On the
81	default settings it squash-merges once the repo's checks pass, so daily lesson-capture never floods review
82	requests while every change still gets a PR trail and a CI gate. This writes only the repo's *own* local
83	packs (not the shared canon). A run that finds nothing and opens nothing is fine — and common.
84	
85	A new check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one — so CI stays green and
86	the PR can merge; a check that can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
87	
88	## Tracking: log each run under the task's own issue
89	
90	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
91	
92	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract**
93	
94	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle, and it
95	differs per repo). A run that finds no issue under the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open,
96	close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no meaning, only the log does. When a run adds a lesson,
97	converts one to a check, or prunes logs, log it as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue — so the issue
98	accumulates a scrollable history, each entry naming **what happened and where**. A run that changed nothing
99	logs nothing. (A repo that still carries a closed `Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract` issue from when
100	the halves were two tasks keeps it as history — never post to it, never reopen it.)
101	
102	## Run on a capable model
103	
104	Deciding whether a lesson is genuinely new and durable — and deduping it against what's already documented —
105	is a **judgment call**, not mechanical extraction. A downgraded model adds noise or restates what's there,
106	and **on the default delivery no human reviews the PR before it lands** — CI gates correctness, not whether a
107	"lesson" earns its keep — so the capable-model requirement matters all the more. This task declares
108	`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
109	
110	## What this task must never do
111	
112	- **Never write outside the repo's own local packs** — this task improves the repo's **packs**, never the
113	  canon and never the project's own code. Everything else under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mount, and
114	  lifting a lesson up into the canon is the central promote task's job. A lesson tied to one call site lands
115	  as its pack's entry **naming the site**, not as an edit out there. The `growth-write-scope` check keys on
116	  this run's pinned title (below) and reds any path outside the local packs.
117	- **Never widen past the Context window** — the halves it declares live, the substantive commits and the
118	  touched PRs/issues named there are the scope; do not re-decide it. That includes the upgrade pass: this
119	  run's own additions, never the standing backlog.
120	- **Never merge `conversation-logs`** anywhere, and never rewrite its history — plain add and remove commits only.
121	- **Never paste the conversation onto an issue** — not raw JSONL, not a rendered transcript, not the turns
122	  themselves. Each landed rule gets one ≤200-word summary of the exchange behind it, and nothing more.
123	- **Never delete a log younger than retention, and never delete anything while `retention_days` is unset** —
124	  deletion is the ack that both passes happened.
125	- **Don't add noise** — a duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, the more so when
126	  its PR usually lands with no human review to catch it.
127

1	---
2	name: extract-from-activity
3	description: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from repo activity
7	
8	The **artifact** half of lesson extraction: mine what a window of work left behind — commits, the PRs
9	merged in it, the issue discussion around them — for durable, reusable lessons, and fold each into the
10	repo's **own local packs**. Its sibling [extract-from-conversations](../extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
11	mines the *dialogue*; this one never sees a conversation, only what the work committed.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives are shared with that sibling and stay canonical in
15	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't re-derive it. What follows is only
16	what reading *artifacts* adds.
17	
18	## Capture at the repo's own level
19	
20	Write each lesson at whatever level reads naturally for this repo — refer to its files, services, or
21	mechanics wherever that's what makes the lesson clear. Don't force either extreme: don't contort a lesson
22	to be hyper-specific, and don't polish it into a general, portable rule. Making a lesson portable is the
23	growth lifecycle's **promote** stage, done canon-side later over whatever merged here; here, just capture
24	it usefully and let promotion lift whatever turns out to travel.
25	
26	## Read the window — and read merged PRs properly
27	
28	Work only the window you were handed (a scheduled run gets it as binding scope in the dispatch issue's
29	Context; an owner's ask names it in words). Never widen it.
30	
31	1. **The commits** — full bodies, and the diff wherever a fix is non-obvious.
32	2. **The PRs merged in the window** — read these *first* and read them *whole*: the diff **and** the
33	   review discussion. A merged PR is usually the window's richest lesson source, because it records what
34	   was tried, what a reviewer pushed back on, and why the landed shape won. A verdict reached in review
35	   is a lesson already argued; the commit alone shows only the winner.
36	3. **The issue activity** it names — the comments changed on those numbers.
37	
38	## What artifacts signal — and what they don't
39	
40	The signals worth converting here are the ones an artifact can carry: a fix whose diff is small but whose
41	*reason* is not obvious from the code; a review comment that names a convention the author missed; a
42	revert or a follow-up fix that says the first shape was wrong; a PR that grew several rounds because its
43	approach was re-decided mid-flight.
44	
45	**An already-settled, already-enforced implementation choice is not a lesson.** If a check or a test
46	already pins the shape — which roots a CI sweep walks, which contract a construction must satisfy — and
47	all that is left to say is *why it looks like that*, that explanation belongs as a comment at the
48	implementation site, not as prose in a pack. A rule earns its place by steering a **future** decision or
49	catching a **repeatable** mistake, not by narrating a past one that is already locked in.
50	
51	Wall-time and dialogue friction (a clarifying round-trip, a backtrack, a wait sat through) leave no trace
52	in a diff. Don't infer them from artifacts — that is the conversation sibling's territory, working from
53	logs that actually carry the timestamps.
54	
55	## Landing it
56	
57	Route each keeper down the ladder in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — check first,
58	then pack skill, prose last — into the local pack whose territory owns it. Write more checks and less
59	prose, and keep each addition terse and in the repo's own voice.
60	
61	A new check ships **green or not at all**: see it fail on a violating fixture and pass on a clean one. A
62	rule that cannot be made confident lands as prose instead — never as a broken check.
63	
64	Finding nothing is a perfectly good and common outcome; a duplicate or invented "lesson" is worse than
65	adding nothing.
66

1	---
2	name: extract-from-conversations
3	description: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from a conversation
7	
8	The **dialogue** half of lesson extraction: read one agent ↔ user session — its turns *and* the actions
9	taken in it — and convert its friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less
10	dependent on human steering. Its sibling [extract-from-activity](../extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) mines
11	what the work committed; this one mines how the work went.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives stay canonical in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't
15	re-derive it. What follows is only what reading a *conversation* adds.
16	
17	## The goal
18	
19	Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less rework, less
20	waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but as "where did this
21	cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost next time." If a pass can't name
22	a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's fine.
23	
24	## Where the conversation comes from
25	
26	- **A captured log** on the repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch (`<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`),
27	  read with plain git in the checkout — `git show origin/conversation-logs:<file>`. The log carries
28	  per-entry timestamps, per-message token usage, and the `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs behind every
29	  wall-time number, which is exactly what the measured analysis below needs. This is the routine path.
30	- **The live session**, when an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective. Same method; deliver the
31	  capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**, never one that self-merges.
32	
33	**Never reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner decides
34	when a session is done enough to mine.
35	
36	## What to look for — the friction signals
37	
38	Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop cost more than
39	necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.
40	
41	### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user
42	
43	The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I meant…"); the agent
44	building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose
45	answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.
46	
47	**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every question the
48	user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate **convention or glossary entry**;
49	a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc
50	the agent reads cold and gets right the first time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds
51	correctly **without the round-trip**.
52	
53	### 2. Suboptimal agent actions
54	
55	The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran a command
56	that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light one fit; reinvented
57	something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written to "verify"; missed an existing
58	convention and had it corrected in review.
59	
60	**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing helper/convention
61	so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read** (the usage-site-vs-central call is in
62	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). The test: next time the agent takes the good path
63	first, not after a detour.
64	
65	### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them
66	
67	The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been parallel; a
68	padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its result was already in
69	hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already green.
70	
71	**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers from the log's own timestamps
72	and separate the kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting**
73	(sleeps, polling, a finished process not yet killed). The numbers are computable, never estimated. A fix is
74	only credible against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
75	was already optimal.
76	
77	**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
78	kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the subject of
79	the standing **efficiency analysis** in [the unattended-agents skill](../unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold
80	a wall-time finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
81	loss of quality.
82	
83	## Encode the questions the user keeps asking
84	
85	The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks *repeatedly* are a
86	checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how many processes ran — could it be
87	fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its work was done?", stop waiting to be asked —
88	fold those exact questions into a **standing self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the
89	relevant work, and close with a terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each
90	recurring question converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
91	retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively, with numbers.
92	
93	## Two passes per log, and the second one may overturn the first
94	
95	A captured log gets a **fresh pass** within a day of capture and a **final hindsight pass** just before
96	retention deletes it, against the corpus as it stands by then. The hindsight pass is a real re-read, not a
97	formality: a friction signal that looked situational the first time may have recurred since, and a lesson
98	landed since may have made a keeper redundant. Both directions are legitimate outcomes.
99	
100	## Provenance: summarize the exchange, never paste it
101	
102	For each rule that actually **lands** from a log, post one short comment on the issue the log names
103	(`--issue-<n>--` in its filename; **`--issue-0--` means the capture had no associated issue**, so there is
104	nothing to post on and the rule simply lands without a comment):
105	
106	- one provenance line — the rule added, the capture date, the session id;
107	- then a **200-word-max** description of just the slice of conversation that caused the rule: what was
108	  asked, what went wrong or got corrected, and why the rule follows from it.
109	
110	**Summarize, never transcribe.** The dialogue itself is far too verbose for an issue — no pasted turns
111	beyond a short quoted phrase, never raw JSONL, never a rendered transcript. A log that yields nothing gets
112	**no** comment: extraction is the only path to permanence, and a log's conversation is gone once retention
113	deletes it. That is a deliberate call, so a padded "lesson" written to feel productive costs more than the
114	silence it replaced.
115

1	# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request
2	
3	How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
4	delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
5	run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
6	the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
7	your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
8	lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.
9	
10	## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest
11	
12	Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:
13	
14	- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
15	  applies to you.
16	- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
17	  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
18	  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.
19	
20	## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference
21	
22	`.claudinite-checks.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:
23	
24	- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
25	- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
26	  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
27	  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
28	- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
29	  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
30	- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
31	  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
32	  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the dispatch issue.
33	
34	## 2. Arm auto-merge
35	
36	Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
37	it once this repo's required checks pass.
38	
39	## 3. When the arm is rejected
40	
41	- **"Pull request is in clean status"** — the base branch requires nothing, so auto-merge
42	  has no queue to wait behind and this arm will be rejected every time. That is a repo
43	  *shape*, not an error — nothing needs fixing, and the merge is yours to make: once any
44	  checks that did start on the PR's head have **concluded green**, merge it yourself
45	  (squash). A repo with no PR checks at all merges as soon as the PR is mergeable.
46	- **Any other rejection** ("auto-merge is not allowed", "unstable status", …) — judge on
47	  evidence, exactly as the code lane's landing pass does. Read the workflow runs on the
48	  PR's **head sha**:
49	  - A run parked at `action_required` **never ran** — it is neither a pass nor a failure;
50	    ignore it and judge by the runs that actually executed.
51	  - Wait (within your run's time budget) for the real runs to conclude. Everything
52	    concluded, nothing failed, at least one succeeded → merge (squash).
53	  - Anything genuinely failed (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`),
54	    or the runs won't conclude inside your budget, or GitHub refuses the merge itself
55	    (a required gate you could not see) → **leave the PR open** and say why in your
56	    wrap-up comment, naming the repo settings a human should check: Settings → General →
57	    "Allow auto-merge", and Settings → Actions → General workflow-approval requirements
58	    (the usual source of the parked `action_required` run). A PR left open with its
59	    reason stated is a *delivered* outcome within the `merged-pr` ceiling — the trail
60	    survives and the task's next cycle (or the owner) picks it up; a merge past a red or
61	    unseen check does not survive anything.
62	
63	## Never
64	
65	Merge with anything but squash; merge while a real check is failing or still running;
66	arm or merge when the repo said `review`; write `maintenance.delivery` yourself; or
67	manufacture a merge to satisfy the ceiling — "no change" and "left open, reason stated"
68	are always legal outcomes.

content.content:
1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
42	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
43	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
44	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
45	
46	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
47	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits, the lesson lands in the repo's general local pack. A **new** local
48	pack is justified only by the repo's own **project structure** — a segment of the repo's tree whose work is
49	its own territory (a `client` pack for work under `client/`), so a repo's local packs mirror its layout.
50	**Never mint a local pack around a technology or a methodology**, however real the knowledge: capture those
51	lessons in the structural pack that owns the work, and let the canon-side promote stage — Claudinite's call,
52	never a member's — decide whether a technology or methodology facet earns a pack of its own.
53	
54	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
55	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
56	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
57	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
58	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
59	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
60	
61	**Two kinds never become a pack rule, however strong the evidence** — filter on what the lesson is *about*
62	before picking a mechanism. (1) **The owner's own preferences** — which word authorizes a merge, tone, how a
63	summary is shaped. They belong to the person, are injected per session from their own preference file, and
64	change without any repo hearing about it; a pack copy goes stale silently and then contradicts the live one.
65	(2) **The agent framework's own loading mechanics** — which packs are declared, why a skill didn't mount, why
66	an injection missed. That's engine plumbing, not project knowledge: a real defect there is filed upstream, and
67	writing it down as a project rule preserves the bug instead of fixing it.
68	
69	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
70	
71	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
72	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
73	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
74	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
75

capture-log: retry the tip reads, not only the push (#810)

The retry loop protected only the push, so a transient proxy outage on the
ls-remote that opens every attempt threw straight out of the loop and dropped
the capture. A SessionEnd capture is its session's only chance — no later merge
capture picks up a session that never merges — so both network reads now cost
an attempt rather than the run, and the exhaustion error names what was
actually refused.

docs/ is outside the vendor set, so any reference to it from a pack file
resolves to nothing in every consumer — the reference-integrity class that

work-scoped, so it only sees paths the branch itself deletes, and docs/ is

vendor walk carries: packs/README.md and packs/directory.GENERATED.md sit
directly under packs/ and are not vendored, so they fall outside the guarded
region structurally rather than through a hand-maintained carve-out. A pack's
own docs/ subdirectory resolves file-relative and reads as a self-reference.

The full design record for replacing the slot scheduler with a pull-based
work-item queue, under the owner's standing-item model: the tick creates
each task's item unconditionally at its anchor and evaluates nothing; the
precondition runs once per period at pick, on the executor; a no-go rolls
the item to its next anchor, so the item itself carries "asked, declined,
wakes at T". No slot ids, no run-ledger watermark, no exclusive claim, no
label-event re-arm; forcing is waking the standing item.

making every scenario executable — 39 tests in CI, a coverage map tying
each design decision to its validating test, and "The unsimulated world"
naming every boundary the model does not cover. The simulator caught six
real spec bugs prose replay missed (F13 occurrence-guard double
execution, F14 the invisible stuck dependency, F15 the pick-filter race,
F16 duplicate standing items from stale lists, F17 the leash livelock,
F18 lifetime-scoped claim arbitration) — all fixed in the design and
pinned by tests. Migration plan tracked in #801.

- The canary rehearsal gate had been vacuous since the canary flipped — it drove

  convergence marker.
- #786: freshness measured by version for updates-served members.
- #787: an update PR that cannot land in-cycle is disposed of before the next
  converge, not left for a duplicate to stack on.
- #798: the apply stage is asked for by records that declare `applyStage`, not by
  any version number moving — a mechanical migration no longer costs an agent
  session on every member.
- #797: workflow convergence restored. Workflow-bound content is withheld to
  `.claudinite/pending-workflows/`, which the Action token can push, and delivered
  by the apply stage. Also makes the `CLAUDINITE_CAN_WITHHOLD_WORKFLOWS`
  announcement true, closing a latent defect that would have failed the whole
  update cycle on the first record materializing a workflow.

sheepdog: merge fleet-census and fleet-freshness into one roster sweep (#792)

The two tasks walked the same fleet and classified the same repos twice,
from two independently-maintained pieces of code: each had its own
enumeration, owner filter, empty-enumeration guard, structural skips and
declaration read per repo. The freshness sweep's header claimed it "takes
coverage as given" while re-deriving it on another cadence in another
process, and the two classifications had drifted apart — `exclude` was
applied at different points, so an excluded repo still carrying a
declaration read `covered` to one and `out of scope` to the other, and
each half's `unknown` failed its own run knowing nothing of the other's.

`fleet-roster` replaces both: one enumeration, one declaration read per
repo, one roster, two views over it. The issue families stay distinct —
`fleet-adoption` and `fleet-drift` close on unrelated conditions — and
each keeps its own module, convergence policy and report section.

`unknown` is now per-question: an unreadable declaration is unknown to
both halves, a failed mount probe to the freshness half alone, since the
coverage verdict was already made from a declaration that read fine.
Either fails the run, so nothing is downgraded to silence.

Daily, including the freshness probe. That costs roughly two extra REST
reads per covered member on the six days that were coverage-only; it is
not an API-call saving and is not claimed as one. The alternative was
half a task computing its own weekly gate, which would reimplement
dueness. convergeDrift's silence on an unchanged verdict is what keeps
the faster cadence quiet.

The drift-issue body marker still spells `fleet-freshness`, pinned by a
test: every open drift issue carries that string, and renaming it would
read them all as `unrecorded` and comment a spurious verdict change.

file unchanged and is untouched here. The per-project-scheduling,
task-prework and skill-usage-metrics DESIGN docs keep their references to

1	# Claudinite — the canon's own non-portable working rules
2	
3	This is the Claudinite home repo's own local pack: the capture surface for lessons that are
4	**specific to working on the canon itself** and would not make sense mounted into a consuming
5	project. Portable lessons — anything true for repos beyond this one — belong in the shared canon
6	under `packs/`/`skills/` instead (proposed by PR, or lifted by the promote stage).
7	
8	The growth lifecycle writes here automatically: the `growth-extract` daily task routes the canon's
9	own non-portable lessons — mined from repo activity and from captured conversations alike — into
10	this pack (each at the local promotion ladder's strongest mechanism — a check where the rule is deterministic, otherwise terse
11	prose below).
12	
13	## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate
14	
15	- **`canon-curation` lives in `.claudinite/local/packs/`, not `packs/`** (owner decision,
16	  2026-07-19). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite —
17	  project-specific content on the home's own capture surface. Do not propose moving it back, and
18	  do not describe the move as open or provisional.
19	- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is ON — the fleet's default path** (same decision). The
20	  planner reads every member's local-pack daily descriptors by default; never reintroduce an
21	  "experimental / not enabled" framing or an opt-in seam for it.
22	- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** Any rule about what the `packs/`
23	  tree may reference is expressed by declaring/configuring the `barriers` pack (contributed
24	  edges, `siblings`/`scope` capabilities — extend barriers generically if a capability is
25	  missing). Never write standalone code that checks packs-tree segregation.
26	- **A `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` records the mechanism only** (owner decision, 2026-07-23,
27	  #420). Status, phase tracking, in-flight-PR reconciliation and remaining work live in that
28	  initiative's tracking issue (task-prework → #394); a phased plan lives in the sibling
29	  `MIGRATION.md`. Don't reintroduce a status / open-questions / remaining-work section there.
30	- **Multi-session work hands off through the tracking issue, never a prepared prompt** (owner
31	  correction, 2026-07-23). The owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`, so state not written
32	  into the issue is lost. Before ending a session on unfinished work, update the issue and let
33	  the session summary be a pointer to it — never compose a bespoke "pick up from here" prompt.
34	- **The canon never knows which repos consume it — fleet-wide aggregation is Sheepdog's domain**
35	  (owner correction, 2026-07-28, #520). Designing anything that spans repos, the tempting shape is
36	  a member list (or a "fleet" task) living in the canon. It doesn't go here: the canon carries only
37	  **mechanisms exercised on itself**, and the knowledge of *which* repos exist stays in the
38	  **Sheepdog** repo and its pack, which enumerates members at runtime from its own
39	  `.claudinite-checks.json` entry — exactly where the `fleet-roster` sweep already keeps
40	  it. So a cross-repo feature splits in two: a self-contained per-repo half in the canon, and the
41	  aggregation half as a Sheepdog fleet task. **No repo list exists anywhere in canon code** — and a
42	  derived fleet artifact lands in Sheepdog as a daily **auto-merged PR of a `GENERATED` file**,
43	  never a direct commit to its `main`.
44	- **A pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's
45	  config** (owner ruling, 2026-07-28, #527/#528). An adoption question whose recommended answer is
46	  right for nearly everyone is "bad noise": it taxes every adopting repo to re-state the default,
47	  and materializing that answer into `.claudinite-checks.json` freezes a copy that then drifts from
48	  the pack and has to be migrated. Keep the default in the pack's own code, ask nothing, and let the
49	  rare project that wants to differ add the setting by hand. Read config as *optional* — an unset
50	  key means "the default", never "misconfigured" (`retention_days` unset is precisely why the
51	  growth-extract retention prune is skipped rather than failing).
52	
53	- **What Claudinite ships must run on the credentials and settings a member already has**
54	  (owner ruling, 2026-08-06). Requiring a member to flip a platform setting, or to provision a wider
55	  credential (a PAT, an app installation, a new secret), is a last resort — not because it is hard,
56	  but because it is per-repo manual work that reliably does not happen: the capability is then
57	  quietly dead in every repo nobody configured, indistinguishable from a Claudinite bug, while the
58	  automation's own report says nothing is wrong. Three members filed issues asking for the same
59	  Actions approval setting (ClaudiniteWebsite#95, EdFringeNow#205, TLDR#182); none was changed, and
60	  each repo's converge kept succeeding while its mount fell a day behind. Prefer the route that
61	  works with the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` and stock configuration even when it is less direct,
62	  and where a platform behaviour blocks you, neutralise its *effect* rather than asking for the
63	  platform to be reconfigured. Where no such route exists — a capability the default credential
64	  cannot hold at all, which is why `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` is legitimate — take the requirement
65	  deliberately: name the exact scope, say why nothing weaker suffices, and have the automation
66	  report when it is missing rather than silently degrading.
67	
68	- **A change to what members receive is not verified until a member has received it — force that in
69	  the same session** (owner requirement, 2026-08-06: *"We're not waiting till tomorrow to see if
70	  something worked"*). Merging to canon is evidence about canon; the only thing that exercises a
71	  canon change end to end is a member's converge, and on a daily slot that is a day away — so a
72	  session that closes on "it reaches the fleet tonight" has shipped an unverified change and hands
73	  the owner a question they will ask anyway (asked five separate ways across 2026-08-05/06:
74	  *"Check status"*, *"Did the Sheepdog baselining work?"*, *"check now"*, *"How do you know 'the
75	  fleet is now fully on 076c029'?"*, and forced baselines appended to three consecutive `lgtm`s).
76	  After landing anything that alters what baselining delivers, drive Sheepdog's `fleet-baseline`
77	  workflow with `follow` and report what it did per member, unasked. Two corollaries. **A dispatch
78	  is not a result** — the API's 204 means queued. And **attaching a member repo to the session is a
79	  read you already have**, so attach the repos the verification needs rather than offering to: *"2
80	  of 11 members confirmed … say the word and I'll attach and verify"* bought a round-trip, one of
81	  four the owner spent that morning telling this session to attach repos.
82	
83	- **A code deprecation rides the standard `@deprecated` tag — never a bespoke conformance check**
84	  (owner ruling, 2026-08-09, #707). Retiring a field, option or module does not earn its own rule
85	  module, test file and catalog row: that is machinery to say what one JSDoc line says, and it grows
86	  once per retirement forever. `deprecated-session-scope` was authored as a `basics` check and deleted
87	  the same day it was reviewed (*"I don't think we want to add a check for every code deprecation"*).
88	  Put `@deprecated` on the **definition** — the one place the thing is declared, here the
89	  `session_scope` section of `engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs` — and have each sanctioned holdout
90	  pacify the warning with a comment at its own declaration site saying why it still carries the field.
91	  Keep the contract **validating** the lingering field either way: validation catches a typo that would
92	  otherwise strand a dispatch, and is not the same thing as a conformance rule.
93	
94	## Canon-specific gotchas
95	
96	- **Baselining backfill skips the home.** The nightly baselining that lands a `seededByDefault`
97	  pack (and canon-delivered declaration changes) on every member is gated `!isHome`, so the canon
98	  home is the one repo it never reaches: what the fleet receives automatically, this repo's own
99	  `.claudinite-checks.json` only ever gets by hand.
100	- **Pack discovery imports the whole pack tree eagerly — declaration is irrelevant.**
101	  `discoverPacks` imports every `packs/<name>/pack.mjs` on disk and `scanSkillChecks` imports
102	  every `<pack>/skills/<skill>/checks.mjs` beside it, *before* activation is consulted. So
103	  anything in that import graph loads in every repo under every declaration, and a module that is
104	  also a CLI entry point gets re-imported while it is still evaluating: a top-level `await` in its
105	  entry block then never settles and Node exits 13 having run nothing (#581 — `interview.mjs
106	  check` deadlocked fleet-wide, invisible because the SessionStart orchestrator's fail-soft reads
107	  it as a merely-absent note). Start the work *after* evaluation completes — `check(…).catch(…)`.
108	  Enforced by `pack-discovery-entry-await`; the corollary it can't check is to keep these modules
109	  import-light in the first place.
110	- **A pack's `RULES.md` is injected into every session that declares the pack — an idea nobody can
111	  act on belongs in `docs/`, and a pack file must not link there.** Deferred directions, blocked
112	  proposals and status live in `docs/` (e.g. `docs/future-directions.md`) precisely because pack
113	  prose costs context in every consumer session. And the pointer cannot go the other way: `docs/`
114	  is outside the vendor set, so a link from any file under `packs/` resolves to nothing in every
115	  consumer — the `reference-integrity` class that reached `main` unnoticed in #424 (and that
116	  check is work-scoped, so it only sees paths the branch itself deletes). Reference `docs/` from
117	  the issue or PR instead.
118	- **A pack's `RULES.md` carries directives an agent must obey — never a walkthrough of how the
119	  feature works** (owner correction, 2026-08-06: *"Rules are context for any agentic work, not for
120	  random explanations"*). The same injection that makes the prose useful makes description
121	  expensive: a paragraph that only *describes* a mechanism is paid for by every session in every
122	  declaring repo and steers none of them. Shipping the fleet-baseline `follow` half, the rule the
123	  change actually added was one sentence — the two extra PAT read scopes a followed run needs —
124	  and everything around it was a feature tour. Behaviour description goes in the module header and
125	  the pack `README.md`, read by whoever works on that code rather than loaded ambiently; the test
126	  before a paragraph goes in is whether an agent could *act* differently for having read it. Same
127	  instinct as the comment rule `basics` now carries (describe the current state, not the change),
128	  applied where the cost is per session rather than per reader.
129	- **Pick a scheduled task's cadence from how often its signal actually moves.** On a member the
130	  mounted canon changes most nights — baselining converges `.claudinite/shared/` daily — so any
131	  precondition reading `sharedMount` fires nearly every night, spending an opus dispatch per
132	  firing. Where the work isn't latency-sensitive (pruning, dedup), a stale item stays harmlessly
133	  correct, so daily buys noise, not freshness: `growth-dedup` moved to `weekly` in #583 and loses
134	  nothing, because the signals are window-scoped (`sinceIso`) and `windowStart` widens to the
135	  widest due task's period — a weekly run sees all 7 days, batched rather than dropped.
136	- **The home doesn't declare `git-github`, so its skills never mount — never conclude "no such
137	  skill" from `.claude/skills/`.** `mount-skills.mjs` filters on the *literal* declaration
138	  (`isActive(p, { packs: declared })`), not the `requires` closure `check_the_world.mjs` resolves,
139	  and the baselining that would normalize that closure into `.claudinite-checks.json` is the one
140	  thing gated `!isHome` — so `merge-to-main` and `git-github-advanced` are simply absent here.
141	  Read `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree — the corpus *is* this repo,
142	  and an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. The seeding gap above
143	  is a different one (`git-github` arrives by closure, never `seededByDefault`); catching this
144	  one needs `resolveDeclaredPacks` compared against the literal declaration.
145	- **The same blindness on the member side: a session sees only the packs its repo *declares*, so never
146	  conclude from the mount that no canon pack owns a lesson.** A member's `.claudinite/shared/packs/`
147	  holds its declared set, not the canon — so a pack the repo doesn't declare is simply absent, and the
148	  honest-looking reading ("nothing here covers this") is wrong in the one direction that costs most:
149	  the lesson gets homed in a **new local pack** on the member, duplicating canon territory. Measured
150	  2026-08-09 on EdFringeNow: the client-side data-caching rules that belonged to `static-website` went
151	  into a fresh local pack (whose `ruleRoutingGuidance.belongs` ran 31 words against the 20-word cap, so
152	  the session's own selftest was red), because the repo carries no `site.config` and doesn't declare
153	  the pack — nothing in the session pointed at it. The owner did, by URL: *"That pack does exist … move
154	  the changes into that pack and cleanup the EdFringeNow rules."* Since #728 every mount carries
155	  `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`, the catalog of **every** canon pack — read that, not the mounted
156	  subset, before homing a lesson locally. And when the owning pack's territory is merely too narrow,
157	  **widen its `belongs`** rather than route around it: #727 widened `static-website` by two words,
158	  "shipping" → "shipping and serving", and the rules landed where they belonged. (Portable — a promote
159	  candidate for `grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md`, whose "route to the pack whose territory
160	  owns it" step assumes that pack is visible from the session.)
161	- **Never re-serialize a repo's JSON config to apply an edit — patch the text.** A round-trip
162	  rewrites what it wasn't asked to: Python's `json.dump` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True` (every
163	  non-ASCII character becomes a `\uXXXX` escape), and indent, key order and the trailing newline
164	  become the serializer's opinion. Nothing fails and tests stay green, so it rides onward. Edit
165	  JSON as anchored text; if you must round-trip, pin every lossy default and read the resulting
166	  diff before committing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `repo-text-sweeps`, where a
167	  `\uXXXX`-in-tracked-JSON check would carry it.)
168	- **Test git fixtures must commit with signing off.** `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s `makeRepo`
169	  overrides identity but not signing, so all 31 call sites route fixture commits through the
170	  signing service; when it degrades, each commit blocks on it and the suite leaks descriptors
171	  (~800 per full run against a 4096 cap) until `git commit` and `git push` fail process-wide.
172	  Commit with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`: signing a tmpdir throwaway
173	  buys nothing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `writing-tests`.)
174	- **A canon session with a consumer repo also in its sources will reach for the *consumer's*
175	  merge skill — merge by the skill of the repo you are merging into.** Canon work is routinely
176	  dual-repo (the canon plus the fleet member being piloted), and both repos ship a merge skill
177	  under different names — the canon's `packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/` and, say, GCEC's
178	  local `merge-and-ci`. The consumer's skill wins the match on name/description and is followed
179	  to the letter, so the canon-only steps in *its* recipe are silently skipped — repeatedly, the
180	  **post-merge conversation capture** (`node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue
181	  <n>`, the "After the merge" section of `merge-to-main`). So: before merging in a dual-repo
182	  session, resolve the merge skill **by target repo**, not by which skill matched first — and
183	  treat capture as part of the merge, not as an optional epilogue.
184	- **Fail-soft SessionStart steps hide their own breakage fleet-wide — test the emitted
185	  output, not the exit code.** Every `engine/pack_loader/` SessionStart step
186	  (`inject-pack-prose.mjs`, `mount-skills.mjs`, `env-requirements.mjs`) wraps its body in
187	  `try { ... } catch {}` so a broken loader never blocks a session. That fail-soft is deliberate,
188	  but it means a runtime fault — a wrong dynamic-import target, a renamed module — exits 0 and
189	  simply emits nothing: no error, no signal. And because the engine is vendored verbatim into
190	  every member, one canon regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet at once.
191	  So a step like this must be guarded by a regression test that runs the real script against a
192	  real corpus and asserts the **positive** effect — prose IS emitted — never merely that
193	  `status === 0` (which fail-soft makes meaningless); see
194	  `engine-tests/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.test.mjs`.
195	- **The nightly self-refresh cannot repair the vendor-set computation — pin operational

482	  gets `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml` written into `.github/workflows/` by its nightly
483	  converge; the canon has no mount and no converge, so its own copy is hand-maintained and drifts from the
484	  stub it ships. That drift is invisible until it is a permission denial in production: the canon's
485	  workflow sat on `actions: read` while the stub had carried `write` since store-release, so the CI
486	  dispatch POST 403'd and **only** the canon's own fold PR stranded — for ten days (#535, fixed in #704).
487	  Paired tests over the two files are not the safety net you think: one already asserted the
488	  `overrides` input on both and said nothing about `permissions`, so the drift walked straight past it.
489	  So when a change touches the vendored stub, edit the canon's `.github/workflows/` copy in the **same
490	  commit** and diff the two whole files, never just the lines you came for.
491	- **Never combine PRs by pushing one's branch onto the other's base — update the PR you're keeping,
492	  close the other** (owner decision, 2026-08-11). GitHub marks a PR merged the moment its head is
493	  reachable from its base, so the push merges it under your name and shows it merged into a branch

497	  work that completes or corrects an open PR belongs on that PR's branch. Splitting it gives the owner
498	  two gates for one decision and invites approving half — #739's new pack was approvable while
499	  `basics` still held a rule the pack owned.
500	- **A held stamp reads as stale if you judge a member by `claudinite.updated` alone — read `ref`
501	  too.** `heldStamp()` pins a repo's `updated` to the day before its earliest pending agentic note
502	  (#330), so a mount converging normally every night can still show a week-old `updated` for as
503	  long as that note stays unapplied — which is the mechanism working, not a sign of a dead repo.
504	  Misread live 2026-08-12 (#768): a session called ClaudiniteCanary and GoogleCalendarEventCreator
